sources.entry: Stalwart Mail Server - All-in-one mail server with JMAP, IMAP4, and SMTP support and a wide range of modern features. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Rust/Docker
Stalwart | All-in-one mail and collaboration server (JMAP, IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV) written in Rust

summary.one_liner: Stalwart is an open-source, Rust-based all-in-one mail and collaboration server supporting JMAP, IMAP, POP3, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV.
summary.what_it_does: Stalwart provides a mail server with JMAP, IMAP4rev1/rev2, POP3 and SMTP support, plus ManageSieve and Sieve scripting. The SMTP side includes built-in DMARC, DKIM, SPF and ARC, DANE, MTA-STS and TLS reporting, and automated DKIM key rotation. It bundles a spam and phishing filter with DNSBL, Pyzor, greylisting, reputation monitoring and optional AI classifiers. Collaboration features cover CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV file storage, each with JMAP equivalents and sharing/ACL support. The README also lists pluggable storage backends (for example PostgreSQL, SQLite, RocksDB, S3-compatible), full-text search, OIDC/LDAP/SQL authentication, ACME certificate provisioning, a web-based admin dashboard, and clustering options. Some of these capabilities, such as multi-tenancy, SCIM and sharded storage, are described as Enterprise-edition features.
use_cases: replace separate mail, calendar and contacts servers
run a mail server for a small team or organization
spam and phishing filtering for mail
sync calendars and contacts with CalDAV/CardDAV clients
host shared file storage over WebDAV
how_to_run: Install Stalwart on Linux, macOS or FreeBSD following the instructions at stalw.art/docs
Install on Windows following the platform instructions
Run using Docker following the Docker instructions
notable: Implements JMAP, IMAP, POP3, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV in one server
Built-in spam filter with DNSBL, Pyzor, greylisting and optional AI classifiers
Automatic ACME TLS certificates and DKIM key rotation
Pluggable storage backends including PostgreSQL, SQLite, RocksDB and S3-compatible
Dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 and a proprietary Enterprise license
caveats: Some features (multi-tenancy, SCIM provisioning, sharded storage, live telemetry) are reserved for the proprietary Enterprise edition
Only vouched contributors may open pull requests, and only bug fixes and translations are accepted for now
The README does not describe a fixed set of platform limits beyond the listed install targets
